rules.statement: A gift that includes a promise not to raise any dispute and a provision allowing the donee to deal with the property as they please is revocable, unless there are clear words of renunciation.
rules.supporting_quote: "But in this case Schneider J., in referring to the 1858 case of Kiri Menika v. Cau Rala, appears to have relied on the report in Lorenz as to the provisions of the deed in the 1858 case, and to have thought therefore that in the 1858 case the Full Bench had held that the words 'to be possessed finally as paraveni property' constituted a renunciation of the right of revocation. But I have already pointed out that in fact (as stated later by Wood Renton J.) the deed in the 1858 case contained three provisions, and not merely the single provision 'that the donee shall possess for ever'."
